concerns.text: T018 implements a grid search for trees (10-50) and max_depth (≤10). The spec (FR-003) and plan (Phase 6) mandate a fixed 'suitably large number' of trees (500) and do not authorize hyperparameter tuning. This task silently relaxes the model specification, risking failure to meet SC-001 (R² ≥ 0.6) and violating the deterministic nature of the plan.

FR-006 explicitly requires a 'two-tailed t-test on permutation importance scores'. T024 and T058 implement 'empirical p-values' derived from the permutation distribution and Holm-Bonferroni correction, but omit the specific t-test mandated by the spec. This is a semantic weakening of the statistical validation requirement.

T068 verifies 'all permutation-importance p-values < 0.05'. However, T025 applies Holm-Bonferroni correction, which adjusts the significance threshold per feature. Verifying against the raw 0.05 threshold ignores the correction required by the methodology, effectively weakening the statistical rigor (SC-003) by validating against the wrong criterion.

FR-004 requires reporting the 'associated p-value' for the Pearson correlation on the held-out set. T020 mentions computing R², MAE, RMSE, and generating plots, but does not explicitly include the computation of the Pearson p-value (via bootstrap as per plan/research) in its deliverable description. This risks dropping an acceptance criterion.

T109 proposes a stability check script that compares top-5 rankings across runs. While SC-006 requires this stability, the task description suggests using 'different seeds (or fixed seeds with shuffled splits)'. Constitution Principle I (Reproducibility) and the plan's emphasis on fixed seeds for reproducibility conflict with 'different seeds' for the primary stability check. The task must strictly enforce fixed seeds with shuffled splits or a defined deterministic variation to avoid violating reproducibility principles.
